events.title: Jacob sees Esau coming and arranges his family
events.narrative_summary: Jacob looks up and sees Esau coming with four hundred men. He divides the children among Leah, Rachel and the two maidservants, putting the maidservants first and Rachel and Joseph last.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Follows the morning after the wrestling (32:31-32), so anchored on the END of the sunrise scene; a short arrangement of the camp, 20 minutes, margin 3 hours since the text does not say how soon Esau appears. Tier DAY_SEQUENCE: the continuous day of the encounter.

events.title: Jacob bows seven times and Esau embraces him
events.narrative_summary: Jacob goes ahead of his family and bows to the ground seven times as he nears his brother. Esau runs to meet him, embraces and kisses him, and they weep.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous with the arrangement of the camp (33:3 'he passed on before them'); anchored on its END. Seven prostrations plus a run take about 20 minutes.

events.title: Jacob presents his wives and children to Esau
events.narrative_summary: Esau asks who the women and children are, and Jacob answers that God has graciously given them. The maidservants, then Leah, then Joseph and Rachel come forward and bow.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous after the embrace; anchored on its END, 20 minutes for the three groups to approach and bow.

events.title: Esau accepts Jacob's gift after urging
events.narrative_summary: Esau asks about the droves he met; Jacob says they are to find favor with him. Esau says he has enough, but Jacob urges him and he takes the gift.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous conversation, anchored on the END of the presentation; 30 minutes.

events.title: Jacob declines Esau's company and says he will follow to Seir
events.narrative_summary: Esau proposes that they travel on together; Jacob pleads that the children and nursing flocks cannot be driven hard and says he will come to Seir at their pace. Esau offers to leave some of his men, and Jacob declines.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous conversation, anchored on the END of the gift scene; 30 minutes.

events.title: Esau turns back toward Seir
events.narrative_summary: Esau returns that same day on his way to Seir.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'On that day' (33:16): starts at the end of the conversation the same day. Duration 6 hours is an estimate for the day's departure; Seir is about 287 km away in a straight line, so the journey itself is far longer and is not counted.

events.title: Jacob journeys to Succoth and builds a house and shelters
events.narrative_summary: Jacob travels to Succoth, builds himself a house and makes shelters for his livestock, and the place is named Succoth.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Starts a day after the parting (margin 1 day) to allow Jacob to break camp. The text gives no duration; building a house and booths implies months, and Targum Pseudo-Jonathan says he stayed there twelve months, so duration is 1 year. Shechem is about 32 km from Succoth, within a day's travel, so the length comes only from the stay.

events.title: Jacob arrives safe at Shechem and camps before the city
events.narrative_summary: Jacob comes safely to the city of Shechem in Canaan, on his return from Paddan-aram, and camps before the city.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Anchored on the END of the Succoth stay. Succoth to Shechem is 32 km straight, about 40 km by road; by donkey about 1 day (urim travel, 4 km/h, 10 h moving). Margin 3 months because the length of the Succoth stay is uncertain.

events.title: Jacob buys a field from the sons of Hamor
events.narrative_summary: Jacob buys the plot where he pitched his tent from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, for a hundred kesitah.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word; a purchase made after pitching the tent, estimated within days of arrival: anchored on the END of the arrival, margin 7 days, 2 hours for the transaction.

events.title: Jacob sets up an altar called El-Elohe-Israel
events.narrative_summary: Jacob erects an altar on the purchased land and calls it El-Elohe-Israel.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word; follows the purchase on the same land, anchored on its END with a margin of 7 days and about a day for the building.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: God promised Jacob at Bethel 'I will keep thee ... and will bring thee again into this land' (28:15); Jacob 'came safe' to Shechem 'in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-aram' (33:18), the return the promise foretold.

Jacob prayed to be delivered from the hand of Esau (32:11), and at the meeting he credits God's grace for Esau's friendly welcome: 'thou wast pleased with me' (33:10) and 'God hath dealt graciously with me' (33:11); the embrace in place of an attack (33:4) is the answer he recognizes.
Jacob sent the droves to appease Esau and 'find favor' (32:20), and Esau takes the gift after urging (33:11).
Owning the plot where he had pitched his tent (33:19) lets Jacob set up an altar there (33:20).

entities.etymology_meaning: 'El, the God of Israel', or 'God is the God of Israel'; Israel here is Jacob's new name (Gen 32:28).
entities.summary_bio: The altar Jacob sets up on the field he bought at Shechem and names with a title of God (Gen 33:20). The name claims the God of his new name as his God.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'bene Hamor', 'sons of Hamor'; a collective for his family and household.
entities.summary_bio: The family of Hamor of Shechem, from whom Jacob buys a parcel of field for a hundred qesitah (Gen 33:19). They are the landowners who sell to the newcomer.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'helqat hassadeh', 'the portion of the field'.
entities.summary_bio: The plot before the city of Shechem where Jacob pitched his tent and which he bought from the sons of Hamor for a hundred qesitah (Gen 33:19). It is the first piece of land in Canaan the text shows him owning.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Booths' or 'shelters', which the text itself gives as the reason for the name.
entities.summary_bio: A place east of the Jordan where Jacob goes after parting from Esau. He builds a house for himself and shelters for his livestock there, and names the place for them (Gen 33:17).

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew for 'donkey' (a name probably linked to the Hivite/Hurrian setting; donkeys were used in covenant rites at Shechem).
entities.summary_bio: Father of Shechem, named in Gen 33:19 as the man whose sons sold Jacob a field. In Genesis 34 he rules the city of Shechem.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'shoulder' or 'ridge', the same word as the name of the city.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Hamor, mentioned only as his father's son in Gen 33:19. He shares his name with the city, which stands near where Jacob camps.

components.label_value: Dedicated to the God of Israel
components.evidence_explanation: Gen 33:20: Jacob sets up the altar and calls it El-Elohe-Israel, 'El, the God of Israel'.
Gen 33:4: Esau runs to meet Jacob, embraces him, falls on his neck, kisses him, and they weep.

components.label_value: On his way back to Seir
components.evidence_explanation: Gen 33:16: Esau returns that day on his way to Seir.
Gen 33:11: Jacob urges Esau and 'he took it'.
Gen 33:19: Jacob buys the parcel of the field where he had pitched his tent.
Gen 33:17: Jacob journeys to Succoth, builds a house for himself and shelters for his livestock.
Gen 33:18: Jacob arrives at the city of Shechem in Canaan and camps before it.

systems.name: Purchase of land from its owners
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In the ancient Near East land was held by families and sold by agreement, with a price in silver by weight or in a local unit. Foreigners and sojourners could own land only by a purchase from the landholders, which gave a claim recognized by neighbours. Genesis shows the pattern in 23 (Machpelah, at the gate) and here (a field before Shechem).
rules_and_mechanics: The buyer deals with the landholding family, here 'the hand of the sons of Hamor'.
The price is stated and paid: a hundred qesitah, a unit of silver of uncertain weight.
The land bought is a defined plot, 'the portion of the field' where the buyer's tent already stands.
Purchase turns a sojourner's camp into a holding that others recognize.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob sets up an altar on the field at Shechem and calls it El-Elohe-Israel.
system_instances.significance_note: Marks his return to the land with worship and gives God a title that includes his own new name.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob goes ahead of his family and bows to the ground seven times as he draws near his brother.
system_instances.significance_note: A vassal's greeting to a lord, used by Jacob to show submission after twenty years of estrangement; it prepares Esau's warm answer.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Esau runs to Jacob, embraces him, falls on his neck, kisses him, and they weep.
system_instances.significance_note: Esau's welcome answers the fear of 32:7-8, 11 and ends the feud that began with the stolen blessing.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The maidservants with their children, then Leah with hers, then Joseph and Rachel, come forward in turn and bow to Esau.
system_instances.significance_note: The order shows who stands where in Jacob's household, with Rachel and Joseph last and most protected.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob buys the parcel of the field where he had pitched his tent from the sons of Hamor for a hundred qesitah.
system_instances.significance_note: The first land Jacob owns in Canaan; the setting of the events of Genesis 34 and of later burial traditions.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Esau first declines, saying he has enough; Jacob urges him, and Esau takes the gift.
system_instances.significance_note: Accepting the gift confirms the peace; Jacob compares Esau's welcome to seeing the face of God, recalling Peniel.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob builds a house and shelters at Succoth and calls the place Succoth, 'booths'.
system_instances.significance_note: The name keeps his stay in memory; the stop east of the Jordan delays his arrival in the land.

edges.description: Esau runs to meet Jacob, embraces him, falls on his neck and kisses him.
Esau proposes that they journey together, with himself going ahead of Jacob.
Jacob bows to the ground seven times as he draws near his brother.
Jacob buys the parcel of field where he had pitched his tent from the sons of Hamor for a hundred qesitah.
Jacob says the children are tender and the flocks nursing, and asks Esau to go ahead while he follows slowly to Seir.
Seeing Esau come with four hundred men, Jacob divides the children among Leah, Rachel and the two maidservants.
Jacob presses his gift on Esau, who first refuses and then accepts.
Asked who the women and children are, Jacob answers that they are the children God has graciously given his servant.
Jacob sets up an altar and names it for El, the God of Israel.
